en: Itivuttaka 39 Dukanipāta, Second Chapter Thus it was said. This discourse was spoken by the Blessed One while staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. There, the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Monks! “Venerable sir,” those monks replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this: “Monks, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The one who is a speaker and the one who is a doer. These are the two kinds of persons found existing in the world. [The Buddha then spoke in verse: “The one who merely speaks but does not act, Who praises themselves and disparages others— Such a person is far from the goal, And is called a ‘fool’ by the wise. But the one who acts according to the Dhamma, Who does not speak much, yet is steadfast— Such a person is near to the goal, And is called a ‘wise man’ by the wise. Thus spoke the Blessed One. Having said this, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and departed. Then, not long after the Blessed One had left, a certain monk approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and reported what had occurred. The Blessed One, having understood the meaning of this, on that occasion breathed forth this inspired utterance: “Not by mere talk is one a sage; One who does not act is not a sage. But he who practices the Dhamma accordingly, He is a sage, so says the Dhamma. This is what was said by the Blessed One. Elated, those monks rejoiced in the words of the Blessed One. *End of the Thirty-Ninth Discourse in the Second Chapter of the Book of Twos.*
The Discourse on Teaching.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant; thus have I heard:
“Bhikkhus, for a Tathāgata, an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One, there are two ways of teaching the Dhamma according to method.”
Which two?
“See evil as evil”—
this is the first teaching of the Dhamma.
"‘Seeing evil as evil, become disenchanted with it, become dispassionate toward it, and be liberated from it’—
this is the second teaching on the Dhamma. Monks,
these two teachings on the Dhamma occur in turn for the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.”
The Blessed One spoke this matter.
Regarding this, it is said:
“Of the Tathāgata, the Buddha...”
"Behold the figurative expression of one who has compassion for all beings:
two qualities have been proclaimed."
Behold this as evil,
and become dispassionate toward it; then,
with minds dispassionate, [you shall be liberated].
“You shall make an end of suffering.
This matter was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The second [sutta].
